notes.claim: An inverse function takes the output and does the opposite to get back to the input.
To resolve a force at an angle above the horizontal, the sine function gives the vertical component and the cosine function gives the horizontal component.
In one worked example, a 100 N force at 30 degrees has horizontal component 100 N times cos 30 degrees, 86.6 N, and vertical component 100 N times sin 30 degrees, 50.0 N.
The MCA General Engineering Science I syllabus asks candidates to resolve forces in horizontal and vertical components, restricted to the first quadrant.
The MCA Second Engineer mathematics syllabus defines sine, cosine, tangent, secant, cosecant and cotangent and the relationships between them. (added for i2, review fix)
Khan Academy's right-triangle trigonometry unit includes a lesson on the reciprocal trig ratios. (added for i2, review fix)
The two components of a vector together have the same influence as the single vector, so the vector can be replaced by its two components. (added for i2, review fix)
A projectile launched at an angle to the horizontal has an initial velocity with both a horizontal and a vertical component. (added for i2, review fix)
One field table gives conduit offset shrink of 3/16 inch per inch of offset at 30 degrees (a rounded field figure). (added for i2, review fix)
Another conduit table gives 1/4 inch (0.250) at 30 degrees, so field shrink figures at 30 degrees differ between tables (1/4 against 3/16). (added for i2, review fix)
Conduit offset shrinkage is a common field allowance, not a code rule. (added for i2, review fix)
